mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 1 Series 130i engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 1 Series 130i engine replacement typically costs £1,295-£2,800 for a reconditioned or rebuilt N52B30 unit supply-only. With supply and fit, expect £2,500-£3,800 depending on the specialist and location.

mainEntity.name: What engine is in the BMW 130i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW 130i is powered by a 3.0-litre naturally aspirated straight-six petrol engine with the engine code N52B30. It produces 265 hp (195 kW) at 6,600 rpm and 315 Nm of torque at 2,500 rpm. The engine features VALVETRONIC valve management, Bi-VANOS variable valve timing and a lightweight magnesium-aluminium crankcase.

Yes - the N52 engine in the BMW 130i is widely regarded as one of BMW's most reliable engines. Unlike the turbocharged N54 and N20 that followed, the N52 does not have widespread timing chain or high-pressure fuel pump issues. Common problems are limited to oil leaks (valve cover gasket, oil filter housing gasket, oil pan gasket), water pump failure and VANOS solenoid issues - all of which are repairable.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 1 Series 130i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 1 Series 130i engine replacement typically takes 2-3 days for a specialist to complete, including removal of the old N52 unit and fitting the replacement.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 130i and 135i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW 130i and 135i are very different cars despite similar power outputs. The 130i uses a naturally aspirated 3.0-litre N52 producing 265 hp, while the 135i uses a twin-turbocharged 3.0-litre N54 producing 306 hp. The 130i is rear-wheel drive with a naturally aspirated character, while the 135i is also rear-wheel drive but with significant turbocharged torque.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 1 Series 130i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 130i was launched in September 2005 as the flagship petrol model of the first-generation 1 Series. It was the most potent 1 Series of its era, powered by a 3.0-litre naturally aspirated straight-six engine that produced 265 hp - seven horsepower more than the contemporary 330i, 530i and 630i. The 130i represented the pinnacle of BMW's naturally aspirated six-cylinder engineering, featuring lightweight magnesium-aluminium construction, VALVETRONIC valve management and Bi-VANOS variable valve timing. It was the world's lightest six-cylinder production engine at the time. Production ran from 2005 to 2013 across the E81 (three-door), E82 (coupe), E87 (five-door) and E88 (convertible) body styles.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 1 Series 130i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 1 Series 130i is powered exclusively by the N52B30 engine - a 3.0-litre naturally aspirated straight-six that produces 258-265 hp. The N52 is widely regarded as one of BMW's most reliable engines, with far fewer major failure points than the turbocharged N54 and N55 that followed. However, like all modern BMW engines, it has its common issues - primarily oil leaks and cooling system components. Replacement demand for the BMW 130i is relatively low compared to turbocharged BMWs, but when failures do occur, the N52 is a well-understood engine with straightforward solutions. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components and a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Oil Leaks - Valve Cover, Oil Filter Housing and Oil Pan Gaskets
problems.rootCause: The N52 engine uses gaskets that can become brittle and leak over time. The valve cover gasket, oil filter housing gasket and oil pan gasket are the most common leak points. A leaking valve cover gasket can cause oil to drip onto the exhaust manifold, producing a burning smell and white smoke.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve cover gasket and associated seals

repairOptions.longevity: Address oil leaks before they cause further issues

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace oil pan gasket - subframe may need lowering
repairOptions.longevity: More labour-intensive, but necessary if leaking

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new gaskets and seals

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2005-2013 BMW 1 Series 130i is currently valued at approximately £5,000-£12,000 depending on mileage, condition and body style (coupe and convertible models command a premium). This places the 130i in a bracket where a rebuilt engine can be a viable investment for well-maintained examples. If your 130i is worth under £5,000 and the engine has suffered catastrophic failure, evaluate scrap value first. For well-maintained, lower-mileage examples (especially M Sport or coupe models) worth £8,000+, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine with warranty is a sound investment.
problems.recommendation: The N52 is a reliable engine, and oil leaks are the most common issue. Address gasket leaks promptly - a £300-£500 specialist repair is far cheaper than dealing with the consequences of a major oil leak. If you notice white smoke or a burning smell, have the valve cover gasket inspected immediately. Unlike the turbocharged N20 and N54, the N52 does not have widespread timing chain issues, making it a more dependable choice for long-term ownership.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N52B30A BMW 1 Series 130i engine prices

problems.h4: Electric Water Pump & Thermostat Failure - Cooling System
problems.rootCause: The N52 uses an electric water pump that can fail without warning. Unlike belt-driven pumps, an electric pump failure may not be preceded by a visible leak. If the pump fails, the engine can overheat rapidly, potentially causing head gasket failure or worse.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace electric water pump and thermostat
Complete rebuilt unit with new components
repairOptions.longevity: If overheating has caused significant damage

problems.recommendation: Water pump and thermostat replacement is recommended as preventative maintenance around 80,000-100,000 miles. If your 130i has not had the water pump replaced, consider doing so proactively - it's significantly cheaper than dealing with an overheated engine.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt BMW 1 Series 130i engine prices

problems.h4: VANOS Solenoid Issues - Variable Valve Timing
problems.rootCause: The N52's VANOS system uses solenoids to control variable valve timing. These solenoids can become clogged or fail, leading to rough idling, reduced power and engine warning lights.

repairOptions.longevity: If VANOS-related fault codes are present

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new components

problems.recommendation: VANOS solenoid issues are usually repairable without engine replacement. A diagnostic scan will identify if VANOS codes are present. Cleaning or replacing the solenoids is a straightforward job for a specialist.

finalCta.h4: Don't Let Engine Issues Write Off Your BMW 1 Series 130i
finalCta.paragraph: The N52 engine in your BMW 130i is one of BMW's most celebrated naturally aspirated six-cylinders - a reliable, characterful engine that deserves proper maintenance. Oil leaks, water pump failure and VANOS issues are the most common problems, and all are repairable without replacing the entire engine in most cases.
